gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 directly identifies the invalid inference that fixed-domain mesh refinement makes the bounds converge to the whole-space eigenvalue. It states the actual finite-R endpoint limits, explains that they remain a proper interval at fixed R, and gives the necessary joint h_max-to-zero and R-to-infinity repair. This covers both the persistent truncation error and the retained lower-bound correction in the gold concern.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify the false fixed-R convergence claim: refinement removes discretization effects but does not remove finite-radius truncation or the finite-radius Neumann-based lower-endpoint correction. Exact whole-space convergence requires R to tend to infinity as well.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed fixed-R mesh-refinement limit is incorrectly identified with the whole-space eigenvalue; the upper and lower endpoints instead retain finite-radius truncation and lower-bound correction, requiring R to tend to infinity for exact convergence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly gives the finite-R limits of both endpoints, explains why they do not equal the true eigenvalue at fixed R, characterizes the resulting non-shrinking interval, and prescribes the joint mesh-refinement and domain-expansion limit.
